question: When was the 78th anniversary of the Quit India Movement celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**8 August 2020.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **78th anniversary of the Quit India Movement** was celebrated on **8th August 2020**.
 
• The Quit India Movement, also known as the **Bharat Chodo Andolan**, was launched at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee by **Mahatma Gandhi** on **8th August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• The movement is a significant milestone in the Indian freedom struggle, symbolizing the collective determination of the Indian people to achieve independence from British colonial rule.
 
• The slogan **"Do or Die"** became the rallying cry for the movement, inspiring millions of Indians to participate in acts of civil disobedience and non-violent resistance.
 
• The 78th anniversary was marked by various events and tributes across the country, remembering the sacrifices and contributions of freedom fighters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Quit India Movement led to mass arrests and widespread protests, with the British authorities responding with severe repression, including the imprisonment of many leaders of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Despite the crackdown, the movement intensified the demand for independence and set the stage for India's eventual freedom on **15th August 1947**.
 
• The movement highlighted the power of non-violent resistance and mass mobilization in challenging colonial rule and achieving political goals.
 
• Anniversaries of the Quit India Movement continue to be observed as a reminder of the enduring spirit of the Indian freedom struggle and the values of courage, unity, and resilience.
